title.en: Hyperscaler Off-Balance-Sheet Lease and Purchase Commitments
title.zh: 超大规模云厂商表外租赁与采购承诺

description.en: Off-balance-sheet leverage facts from Section IV and footnotes 5, 6, 9: Moody's estimate that hyperscalers have roughly $970B of lease commitments of which about $660B is future leases not yet on balance sheet; the Wall Street Journal tally of $2.4T off-balance-sheet liabilities for Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta ($904B future leases + $1.52T future purchase commitments, mostly chips) versus $604B on-balance-sheet ($356B long-term debt + $248B current leases), with only one-fifth of the $3T recognized; footnote 6 leverage definitions (L1-L4, uncommenced leases x 0.75 present-value approximation, June 2026 data, ex-Amazon: L1 20% -> L2 48%, L3 0.7x -> L4 2.6x); and footnote 9's $500B NVIDIA-chip credit facility with a 25% NVIDIA residual value guarantee (up to $125B of backstops).
description.zh: 来自 Section IV 与脚注 5、6、9 的表外杠杆事实：Moody's 估计超大规模云厂商约有 9700 亿美元租赁承诺、其中约 6600 亿美元为尚未入表的未来租约；华尔街日报对微软、谷歌、亚马逊、Meta 四家的统计——表外负债 2.4 万亿美元（未来租赁承诺 9040 亿美元 + 未来采购承诺 1.52 万亿美元，多为芯片），对应表内 6040 亿美元（长期债务 3560 亿美元 + 当期租赁 2480 亿美元），3 万亿美元数据中心相关义务中仅五分之一入表；脚注 6 的杠杆口径（L1-L4 定义、未生效租约按 0.75 折现近似现值、2026 年 6 月数据、剔除 Amazon 后 L1 20%→L2 48%、L3 0.7x→L4 2.6x）；以及脚注 9 的 5000 亿美元 NVIDIA 芯片信贷安排与 NVIDIA 25% 残值担保（最高 1250 亿美元兜底）。

sections: Section IV. Financial Architecture and Risk

notes: Printed page = PDF page - 2; footnotes 5-6 sit on printed pp. 9-10 (PDF 11-12), footnote 9 on printed p. 13 (PDF 15).

Footnote 6 definitions (verbatim structure): L1 = ratio of debt to debt plus the book value of equity; L2 = ratio of debt plus lease obligations divided by debt plus lease obligations plus the book value of equity; L3 = ratio of debt to EBITDA; L4 = ratio of debt plus lease obligations to EBITDA.
Footnote 6 lease-obligation input: commenced lease obligations plus future uncommenced lease obligations multiplied by 0.75 as a present-value approximation; June 2026 data.

Footnote 6 scope: 'Leaving aside Amazon, whose leases include many warehouses, I aggregate across the other four hyperscalers' - so L1-L4 are ex-Amazon aggregates; the paper writes the leverage symbols in math-italic notation (rows normalize them to L1/L2/L3/L4).
Moody's source cited by the paper: Moody's Ratings (2026a, February), 'Accounting - u.s.: Hyperscalers' reported ai-related lease commitments may understate economic risk'.

WSJ figures are 'a recent analysis by the Wall Street Journal' as cited in Footnote 5; $2.4T + $604B underlies the '$3 trillion in datacenter-related obligations' total, and 'only one-fifth' is currently recognized.

Footnote 9 appears alongside Section V text (PDF p.15) but is within this family's assigned extraction scope (Section IV and footnotes 3-7, 9); it quantifies contingent purchase-financing backstops (NVIDIA residual value guarantee) rather than Hyperion-specific facts.

provenance.quote_en: Moody’s estimates that hyperscalers have roughly $970 billion of lease commitments, of which about $660 billion relates to future leases not yet reflected on balance sheet
A recent analysis by the Wall Street Journal tallies $2.4 trillion in off-balance sheet liabilities for the four large hyperscalers (Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta)
$904 billion in future lease commitments and $1.52 trillion in future purchase commitments, mostly of chips.
This compares to $604 billion in on-balance sheet obligations: $356 billion in long-term debt and $248 billion in current lease obligations.
Only one-fifth of the $3 trillion in datacenter-related obligations are currently recognized on these four companies’ balance sheets.
To compute lease obligations, I sum commenced lease obligations and future uncommenced lease obligations, where I multiply the latter by 0.75 to approximate a present value.
Leaving aside Amazon, whose leases include many warehouses, I aggregate across the other four hyperscalers.

The $500 billion credit facility stood up by Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR in August 2026 to finance NVIDIA chips is a good example.
NVIDIA will provide a 25% residual value guarantee, exposing it to as much as $125 billion of backstops.
Google and Broadcom entered into a similar arrangement to help finance acquisition of its TPU chips.
